faq.q: Where is the wettest place in the world?
faq.a: Mawsynram in Meghalaya, north-east India, is usually named the wettest place, with about 11,870 millimetres of rain a year on average.
asks: Which place gets the most rain?

faq.a: A monsoon is a wind that changes direction with the seasons. In South Asia the summer monsoon blows from the sea and brings months of heavy rain.

faq.q: Why do hills make it rain?
faq.a: When wind meets hills, the air is pushed upwards. Air cools as it rises, and cool air cannot hold as much water vapour, so clouds form and rain falls.

faq.q: How much rain falls in Cherrapunji?
faq.a: Cherrapunji, also called Sohra, is near Mawsynram and is almost as wet. It holds the record for the most rain in one year: about 26,461 millimetres, from 1860 to 1861.
asks: What is the rain record for one year?

faq.q: How do people live with so much rain?
faq.a: The Khasi people grow living root bridges from fig tree roots across rivers, and many wear a knup, a big umbrella of bamboo and leaves worn over the back.

facts: Mawsynram in Meghalaya, India, averages about 11,870 millimetres of rain a year.
Nearby Cherrapunji recorded about 26,461 millimetres of rain between August 1860 and July 1861, a one-year record.
